metadata.title: Writing Someone Else's Pipeline
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week02/term2-week2-video-content.md was named as the source but is NOT on disk; claims traced to inbox/week-01/PROJECT_PIPELINE_REPORT.md, KEYWORD_POPUP_COLLABORATION_SUMMARY.md, JANVI_WORK_SUMMARY.md, README.md; Week 2 first-person facts attested by Janvi's pre-approved narration (2026-10-27)
metadata.note: Project update. Thesis: documenting someone else's pipeline, the code shows what was built but not why; every inferred reason must be confirmed with its author. Credit: the generation pipeline (stages 00-07) and its design decisions are Thejus's; Janvi reviewed and documented it and merged the two papers. Narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-27). WORDING LAW: the definitions are never called verified/accurate/reliable.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required intro line + AI-narration disclosure + Thejus credited.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about writing the methodology for a pipeline I didn't build. This narration is an AI-generated voice. The pipeline is my teammate Thejus's; my work this week was reviewing it and writing it up.

props.command: I'm writing the methodology for my teammate's pipeline. I didn't build it. Where do I start?
output: Summarize each stage from the code

beats.narration_text: Our Medhavy textbook popups come from two halves. Thejus's pipeline generates the definitions. My pipeline reviews them with three AI judges. This week I documented his half, then merged our two papers into one.

beats.role_note: GitHub repo → Claude Code; eight stage cards 00–07 light up in narration order; counter to ~2,500 words.
beats.narration_text: I cloned his repository and used Claude Code to summarize all eight stages, from Wikipedia extraction and filtering, through a G P T four o mini rewrite, to abbreviation scanning, merge and upload. Then I wrote about 2,500 words on it.
beats.visual_intent: GitHub repo → Claude Code; eight stage cards 00–07 light up in narration order; counter to ~2,500 words.

beats.role_note: Abbreviation → category gate (only Molecular Biology and Immunology pass) → Gene Ontology lookup → prompt grounding → definition; a dashed bypass 'lookup fails → still written'.
beats.narration_text: The earlier draft never explained how Gene Ontology was used. I traced it in the code and tested the API myself. For molecular biology and immunology abbreviations, the pipeline fetches the Gene Ontology definition and gives it to the model as grounding. If the lookup fails, the definition is still written, just without it.
beats.visual_intent: Abbreviation → category gate (only Molecular Biology and Immunology pass) → Gene Ontology lookup → prompt grounding → definition; a dashed bypass 'lookup fails → still written'.

show.event: traced in the code · tested the API
category gate: Molecular Biology ✓ Immunology ✓ other ✗

beats.role_note: Two overlapping sets (Wikipedia keywords / abbreviations) with one term in the overlap → 'stage 06 merge: Wikipedia wins'; dashed guess card 'my guess: pipeline quality?'.
beats.narration_text: The hard part was the why. When a term exists both as a Wikipedia keyword and as an abbreviation, the Wikipedia entry wins. Reading the code, I assumed that was about pipeline quality. It sounded right.
beats.visual_intent: Two overlapping sets (Wikipedia keywords / abbreviations) with one term in the overlap → 'stage 06 merge: Wikipedia wins'; dashed guess card 'my guess: pipeline quality?'.

beats.role_note: Guess card struck; real reason card 'definition completeness — confirmed with Thejus'; fuller vs textbook-text bars; caption 'Code shows what was built. It doesn't show why.'
beats.narration_text: It was wrong. When I checked with Thejus, the real reason was completeness: Wikipedia entries usually carry a fuller definition, while abbreviation entries come from just the textbook text. Code shows what was built. It doesn't show why.
beats.visual_intent: Guess card struck; real reason card 'definition completeness — confirmed with Thejus'; fuller vs textbook-text bars; caption 'Code shows what was built. It doesn't show why.'

show.event: real reason: definition completeness, confirmed with Thejus

beats.role_note: Two paper outlines slide into one; checklist: shared introduction · results connect generation → 8,968 reached consensus · consistent terms · stages 00–07 + 10–25; '22 hours'.
beats.narration_text: Then I merged the two papers: one shared introduction, results that connect generation to the 8,968 popups that reached consensus for inclusion, consistent terms, and one stage numbering: zero to seven for generation, ten to twenty-five for review. That was 22 hours.
